name: model-file-cve-map
made_with: AI, by MV2 of Munim, Inc.
description: A consolidated, machine-readable map from public model-file parser/deserialization advisories to (a) the file field an attacker controls, (b) the weakness class (CWE), and (c) the static, no-execution pre-load rule in the model-file-scan tool (munimtechnologies/keras-model-scan) that detects it before any loader runs. Covers pickle, keras (.keras), safetensors sharded-index, ONNX and GGUF. Coverage is stated honestly, including documented gaps and classes that no static file scanner can catch. Every identifier was checked at its source; see each entry's 'verified' field.

coverage_legend.full: a shipped rule flags the exact malformed field or opcode that triggers the advisory
coverage_legend.partial: a shipped rule flags a related signal (e.g. an allowlist miss, an unaligned offset) but not the full condition
coverage_legend.class: a shipped rule covers the weakness class; the citation is representative, not a single CVE
coverage_legend.gap: no shipped rule yet detects this; it is a documented roadmap item for a future detector
coverage_legend.out-of-scope: this class cannot be caught by any static pre-load file scanner (it executes at inference, not load) and is named only so readers are not misled

pickle.note: Pickle executes opcodes on load; REDUCE/BUILD/NEWOBJ paired with a dangerous import is arbitrary code execution. ~95% of confirmed malicious public ML models target this format.

keras.note: A Lambda layer or a crafted config.json can name arbitrary Python callables that run during model loading, even with safe_mode=True on affected versions.

safetensors.note: The tensor body is safe by design (no code execution). Residual risks are header-integrity/polyglot files (CWE-20, no CVE) and path traversal via a sharded-index weight_map that points a shard path outside the model directory (CWE-22).

onnx.note: The graph is data, but a TensorProto external_data 'location' is an attacker-controlled relative path joined onto the model directory, and the download helper extracts tar archives without path checks (CWE-22).

gguf.note: No code-execution surface in the container, but hand-written C/C++ readers have turned malformed header integers into heap out-of-bounds read/write. All triggering values live in the header, so a static pre-load check can flag them. Embedded Jinja chat templates are a separate inference-time class (see out-of-scope entry).

containers: MLmodel (the YAML manifest inside an MLflow model directory)
mlflow.note: MLflow's python_function (pyfunc) flavor names a loader_module that MLflow imports and calls at mlflow.pyfunc.load_model time, and an optional 'code' directory that MLflow prepends to sys.path before that import. A crafted MLmodel manifest can therefore load attacker-controlled modules (CWE-829). This is a manifest/metadata surface: the static detector reads the MLmodel YAML only and never imports or runs the referenced code.

entries.mechanism: A model with a Lambda layer deserialized by an affected Keras version runs arbitrary Python at load time.
entries.trigger_field: Lambda layer in the model config

entries.mechanism: A crafted config.json inside a .keras archive names an arbitrary module and function to call during model loading, bypassing safe_mode=True.

A STACK_GLOBAL opcode whose module/name come from preceding opcodes rather than string literals is not resolved by the scanner, so a malicious global evades detection (scanner bypass enabling RCE on load).
The numpy.f2py.crackfortran._eval_length reduce gadget is not in the scanner's dangerous set, so a pickle using it executes arbitrary code while passing validation.

detector.rule: PKL005 (numpy.f2py reduce-gadget; CRITICAL with a REDUCE/BUILD opcode, else HIGH)

entries.mechanism: numpy.f2py.crackfortran.getlincoef reaches eval() on caller-supplied input, so a pickle that imports it and triggers a REDUCE/BUILD opcode runs arbitrary code; picklescan before 0.0.33 did not list getlincoef and cleared it. This is a second numpy.f2py helper fixed in the same picklescan 0.0.33 release as CVE-2025-71339 (_eval_length).

detector.rule: PKL005 (numpy.f2py reduce-gadget; CRITICAL with a REDUCE/BUILD opcode, else HIGH)

entries.verified: 2026-10-22: confirmed at osv.dev/CVE-2025-71372 and GHSA-rrxm-2pvv-m66x (CVSS 3.1 8.1 / CVSS 4.0 7.6, CWE-502, fixed in picklescan 0.0.33). pickle_model_scan 0.2.0 already detects it: the single numpy.f2py PREFIX classification (PKL005) subsumes the whole subpackage, so one detector covers BOTH CVE-2025-71339 (_eval_length) and CVE-2025-71372 (getlincoef), which picklescan patched as two separate denylist entries.

entries.mechanism: A REDUCE/BUILD/NEWOBJ opcode paired with a dangerous import (os.system, subprocess, builtins.eval, ...) executes code the moment the file is loaded.
entries.affected: any loader that unpickles untrusted input
entries.verified: class, not a single CVE; representative of the pickle RCE weakness

entries.mechanism: An archive member whose name contains '..' or an absolute path is written outside the extraction directory.
entries.affected: any loader that extracts an untrusted archive without path checks
entries.verified: class, not a single CVE; representative of the Zip Slip weakness

entries.mechanism: A sharded-model index (model.safetensors.index.json) weight_map value is joined onto the model directory and opened; an absolute or '..' path reads an arbitrary local file at load time.
weight_map / sharded-index shard path traversal escapes the model directory into an arbitrary file read.
entries.trigger_field: weight_map shard path in the sharded index

entries.mechanism: weight_map shard path traversal in the sharded index escapes the model directory.
A TensorProto external_data 'location' value such as '../../../etc/passwd' is joined onto the model directory, reading a file outside it when external tensors are loaded.
download_model_with_test_data extracts a tar archive without checking member paths, so a malicious tar overwrites arbitrary files (tar slip).
entries.trigger_field: tar member paths in a downloaded model archive

entries.mechanism: An ONNX external-data 'location' path traversal in the tract runtime reads a file outside the model directory.
An oversized metadata_kv_count header value overflows an allocation, leading to a heap out-of-bounds write.
An oversized tensor_count header value overflows, leading to a heap out-of-bounds access.
A bypass of the CVE-2025-53630 fix via the tensor_count header (build b8146).
An oversized metadata array length overflows an allocation, leading to a heap out-of-bounds write.
An oversized metadata string length overruns a buffer (out-of-bounds read/write).
A tensor dimensions product overflows in ggml_nbytes (build b7824), leading to an undersized allocation and out-of-bounds access.
A tensor data offset points past the end of the file, leading to an out-of-bounds read.
A malicious Jinja chat template embedded in GGUF metadata executes at inference time (template rendering), not at file load, so byte-level static file scanning cannot catch it.
entries.affected: runtimes that render untrusted chat templates
entries.verified: named honestly so readers know static file scanning does not cover inference-time template injection

entries.mechanism: pyfunc MLmodel loader_module dispatch, and the 'code' directory prepended to sys.path at load, let a crafted MLmodel manifest import attacker-chosen code
entries.affected: see advisory (NVD CVSS 8.6); no fixed-version range published for this identifier
entries.verified: 2026-10-22: CVE-2026-79721 is NVD CVSS 8.6 HIGH, CWE-829; detector MLF005 ships in keras-model-scan v0.45.0 and reads the MLmodel YAML manifest only (loader_module dispatch plus the 'code' directory prepended to sys.path at load), never importing or running the referenced code
